question: Separate National Commission for Scheduled Castes and National Commission for Scheduled Tribes were established by the __________________ Constitutional Amendment Act.
solution:
The correct answer is __**89th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The 89th Constitutional Amendment bifurcated the Combined National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes into two separate bodies.
 
• The establishment of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes has been done under Article 338.
 
• The National Commission for Scheduled Castes is a constitutional body.
 
• The National Scheduled Tribes Commission has come into existence since 2004.
 
• The Chairman of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes is appointed by the President of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **92nd Constitutional Amendment Act:**

 
 
• **​**Included **four** more languages in the **Eighth Schedule** i.e. **Bodo, Dogri (Dongri), Mathilli (Maithili), and Santhali**.
 
• The **total number** of constitutionally recognized **languages** increased to **22**. 
 
 
 
• **83rd Constitutional Amendment Act:**
 
 
• The **83rd amendment** to the Indian constitution was approved in the **year 2000**.
 
• As a result of this modification, **Article 243M** of the Indian Constitution was altered to **remove** the state of **Arunachal Pradesh**, which is exclusively made up of members of** tribal societies**, from the need that reservation of seats be established in Panchayats for members of SC or ST.
 
• ​The state’s former name, Arunachal Pradesh, was** renamed** to **Arunachal Pradesh Tribal Development Council** under the new law.
 
 
 
• **86th Constitutional Amendment Act:****​**
 
 
• The Right to Education was made a fundamental right by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act 2002.
 
• 86th Constitutional Amendment Act 2002 added **Article 21 A** which declares that the state shall provide free and compulsory **education to all children** aged **six to fourteen years**.
 
• It has made **only elementary education** a **fundamental right** but not a professional of higher education.
